title: Polaris Key feature registry (conformance/parity/features.json)
description: Every SDK-facing Polaris Key feature, with a stable id, the service that owns it, how it is proven, and the typed N/As the registry allows per runtime or trait (PARITY §2.2, §3.1). Hand-written; tools/parity-check.ts validates it against this schema and cross-checks every SDK's parity manifest against it.

reasons.description: The typed-N/A reason enum (PARITY §2.2). A manifest declares `runtime` N/As, which hold wherever the runtime is. An `except` with another reason (`outlet`, `dependency`, `version`) declares where the SDK decides that N/A at run time, and the SDK's `supports()` consults a detector for exactly those pairs (P1b-10). `product` is never declared: it applies to every feature an opt-in service owns, whenever discovery says the service is off. `supports()` also answers `version` for a feature the SDK does not implement yet (`planned`) or does not know.

runtimes.description: Every runtime id a manifest or an allowedNa may name.

traits.description: SDK-wide properties that stand in for a runtime in an allowedNa (e.g. `headless`: the SDK ships no UI toolkit). A manifest opts into a trait by listing it.

families.description: The feature families, in page order (PARITY §5.1-§5.7). One table per family on the parity page.

sdks.description: Every SDK with a parity manifest. The checker reads each manifest from its repo-relative path.

constants.description: The SDK's generated constants module (`pnpm gen constants`). It carries the capability table `supports()` reads, generated from the manifest, and its `CAPABILITY_DIGEST`; the checker fails when that digest is not the manifest's (P1b-10).

file.description: corpus: the file under conformance/corpus/v2/ (a trailing slash names a directory).

family.description: corpus: a case family inside the file (e.g. `releaseRecordCases` in cases.json).

command.description: generated: the drift-gate command that regenerates and compares the output.

wp.description: The work package that adds this proof. A corpus proof whose file or family does not exist yet must name one; the checker enforces the proof once it exists.

runtime.description: A runtime id, a trait id, or `*` (any runtime; only for a reason decided at runtime).

title.description: The capability, as PARITY §5 names it.

service.description: The Worker service that owns the server side, or `sdk` for a client-only feature.
